members.working:
Determine hybridisation of the named element in the product for each reaction.
(i) PCl₃ reacts with H₂O at room temperature to form H₃PO₃ (phosphorous acid). In H₃PO₃, phosphorus is bonded to three oxygens and one hydrogen; the geometry around P is approximately trigonal pyramidal, consistent with sp³ hybridisation.
(ii) Xe reacts with F₂ in ratio 1:5 at 873 K and 7 bar in a Ni vessel. Likely product is XeF₅⁻ or XeF₆? At high temperature and pressure, xenon forms XeF₄ or XeF₆; however, with 1:5 F₂ ratio (i.e., 5 F per Xe), the stable product would be XeF₅⁻ (if anion) or XeF₅ (neutral). Xenon in XeF₅ typically adopts a square pyramidal geometry, which involves sp³d hybridisation (or sees-bonding). Pure sp³ hybridisation (tetrahedral) is not typical for Xe in such fluorides; thus Xe is not sp³ hybridised.
(iii) CoCl₃ reacts with NH₃ to form a coordination complex, likely [Co(NH₃)₃Cl₃] or [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃. Cobalt(III) in an octahedral complex uses d²sp³ hybridisation (or uses ligand field splitting), not pure sp³ hybridisation of the metal centre in the product as a simple molecule. Hence Co is not sp³ hybridised in the product.
(iv) P₄O₁₀ hydrolyses with H₂O to form H₃PO₄ (phosphoric acid). In H₃PO₄, phosphorus is tetrahedral (sp³ hybridised).
(v) P₄ reacts with limited dry Cl₂ to form PCl₃ (phosphorus trichloride). In PCl₃, phosphorus is trigonal pyramidal (sp³ hybridised).
Thus reactions where the named element in the product is sp³ hybridised: (i), (iv), (v). That is 3 reactions.
Answer integer 3.
